source: Written 2026-10-22 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2026 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC26.1.ANR.1: Counting is tested as the next, missing or landing number in a written list (no number chart or number line is shown). Counting by twos is not on this standard and is not used. Counting back by fives appears as a small extension of counting by fives.
notes.NC26.1.ANR.2: Collections are described in words (bags, trays, rows, tens and ones); no picture is needed. Counting equal groups uses 2s and 5s, with some totals above 50 inside the standard range.
notes.NC26.1.ANR.3: 30 questions (10/10/10), whole numbers within 99 only. Q 'Max says 90 is 9 tens... Ana says 8 tens and 10 ones' is deliberately a regrouping stretch: both are right.
notes.NC26.1.ANR.4: Number lines, benchmarks and tens/ones forms are written out in words. Numbers kept within 100. Question 27-type regrouping (14 ones) is used once at difficulty 3.
notes.NC26.1.ANR.5: Every total and every number in a stem is within 20; only a wrong option may be larger (26, 36), when it comes from adding by mistake. Nothing needs a picture: counting on, doubles, making ten and adding three numbers are all written out in words. Word problems cover putting together, taking from or apart, an unknown start or change, and comparing (how many more, and the larger amount).
notes.NC26.1.ANR.7: All numbers stay within 20. A balance scale is described in words (all blocks weigh the same), and an unknown is written as ? and called the ?. Letters are not used.
notes.NC26.1.ANR.8: Pass B for 1.ANR.8: 69 questions, 23 per difficulty. All within 100 (two answers are exactly 100 / 92 from 100 or 94+6). Dollar signs avoided (cents only). Multi-step and missing-number items kept as one-digit/multiple-of-10 changes.
notes.NC26.1.RD.1: 30 questions (10/10/10). Sorting is shown only through lists of objects written out in words and counts; the 'sort up to 20 objects' range is met with groups of up to 20 objects (largest set is 20 toys). Counting, comparing and finding a rule are all asked from the written lists.
notes.NC26.1.RD.2: Picture and object graphs are written out as "each picture stands for 1 child" with the number of pictures per row; data lists are written as comma lists of up to 20 votes. Surveys, graphing and conclusions are asked as concrete choice or counting questions.
notes.NC26.1.SGMR.1: Pass B for 1.SGMR.1: 69 questions, 23 per difficulty, all text only. Shapes limited to triangle, square, rectangle, hexagon, circle and unnamed N-sided closed shapes; solids limited to cube, rectangular prism, cylinder, cone, sphere. No question depends on whether a square counts as a rectangle (square-vs-rectangle items state "not a square" or ask only about shared properties), cone/cylinder rolling is avoided except where the others cannot roll, and 3D vertices and edges are left out as beyond Grade 1.
notes.NC26.1.SGMR.2: Written in words only (no pictures). 69 questions, 23 at each difficulty. Fractions stay at halves and fourths of a whole; no thirds taught (a third appears only as a wrong option).
notes.NC26.1.SGMR.3: Written in words only (no pictures, no standard units). 69 questions, 23 at each difficulty. Several D3 questions have a "cannot tell" trap (two objects each longer than a third), where the key is the thing that can be told.
notes.NC26.1.SGMR.5: Clocks are described in words (hand positions) since no picture can be shown. Elapsed time is limited to a half hour or whole hours later/earlier, per the pass-A flag.
notes.NC26.1.SGMR.6: Only like coins are counted, as the summary says (no mixed collections). Skip counting and exchange questions stay within 100 cents, except two comparison distractors (7 quarters = 175 cents, 45 nickels = 225 cents) that are never asked for.
notes.NC26.1.ANR.6: Written for Grade 1: whole numbers within 20, one idea per question. Subtraction facts and the missing number are included because the standard says "addition and subtraction facts". Doubles and ten-plus facts stay within 20.
notes.NC26.1.SGMR.4: Everything is written out in words (no pictures): lengths come from a stated count of units laid end to end, a described row, or a described way of measuring. Only whole numbers of units are used; no half units, no rulers or standard units. "Measure with one unit repeated" is asked as counted placements or marks.

questions.stem: Count up by ones: 46, 47, 48. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Counting up by ones means 1 more each time. 1 more than 48 is 49.

solve.work: Counting up by ones after 48 gives 49.

questions.stem: Count back by ones: 15, 14, 13. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Counting back by ones means 1 less each time. 1 less than 13 is 12.

questions.stem: Count by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Counting by tens means 10 more each time. 10 more than 40 is 50.

questions.stem: Count back by tens: 60, 50, 40. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Counting back by tens means 10 less each time. 10 less than 40 is 30.

questions.solution: Counting by fives means 5 more each time. 5 more than 20 is 25.

questions.stem: What number comes just before 80?

questions.stem: Mia counts: 10, 20, 30, 40. How does she count?
questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before it, so Mia counts by tens.

solve.work: 10, 20, 30, 40 goes up 10 each time, so she counts by tens.

questions.stem: Tom counts his steps: 37, 38, 39. What number does he say next?

questions.stem: What number is 1 more than 64?
questions.solution: Counting up by ones, the number after 64 is 65.

solve.work: 1 more than 64 is the next counting number: 65.

questions.stem: Which number comes right after 89?
questions.solution: After 89 comes 90. The tens digit goes up and the ones start again at 0.

questions.stem: Count up by ones: ?, 53, 54, 55. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Counting up by ones, the number just before 53 is 52.

solve.work: Counting up by ones, the number before 53 is 52.

questions.stem: A game counts 16, 17, 18, 19 and then keeps going. What number comes next?
questions.solution: After 19 comes 20.

questions.stem: A rocket countdown goes 9, 8, 7, 6. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Counting back by ones, the number after 6 is 5.

solve.work: 9, 8, 7, 6 counts back by ones; next is 5.

questions.stem: Zoe counts back: 60, 59, 58. Which number does she say next?
questions.solution: Counting back by ones, 58 is followed by 57.

questions.stem: There are 20 birds on a wire. One bird flies away. How many birds are on the wire now?
questions.solution: 1 less than 20 is 19.

questions.stem: Which number comes right before 35?
questions.solution: The number just before 35 is 34.

questions.stem: Each box has 10 pens. Sam counts the pens by tens: 10, 20, 30. What does he say for the next box?
questions.solution: Counting by tens, 30 is followed by 40.

questions.stem: What is 10 more than 30?
questions.solution: Counting up by tens from 30 gives 40.

questions.solution: The frog lands on 10, then 20, then 30.

questions.stem: Pick the list that counts up by tens.
questions.solution: Counting up by tens adds 10 each time: 10, 20, 30, 40.

questions.stem: There are 50 grapes. Eli eats 10 of them. How many grapes are left?
questions.solution: 10 less than 50 is 40.

questions.stem: What is 10 less than 70?
questions.solution: Counting back by tens from 70 gives 60.

questions.stem: Rob starts on 40 and hops back 10 at a time. After 2 hops, what number is he on?
questions.solution: He lands on 30, then on 20.

questions.stem: Pick the list that counts back by tens.
questions.solution: Counting back by tens takes away 10 each time: 50, 40, 30, 20.

questions.stem: Each hand has 5 fingers. How many fingers are on 3 hands?
questions.solution: Count by fives: 5, 10, 15.

questions.stem: What number comes after 25 when you count by fives?
questions.solution: Counting by fives, 25 is followed by 30.

questions.stem: You are counting by fives. What number comes just before 10?
questions.solution: Counting by fives goes 5, 10. The number before 10 is 5.

questions.stem: Choose the numbers you say when you count by fives from 0.
questions.solution: Counting by fives adds 5 each time: 0, 5, 10, 15.

questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before.

questions.solution: Each number is 5 more than the one before, so she counts by fives.

questions.stem: What rule do the numbers 15, 20, 25, 30 follow?
questions.solution: Each number is 5 more than the one before.

questions.solution: Count up by ones. 1 more than 109 is 110.

questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before. 10 more than 43 is 53.

questions.solution: Each number is 10 less than the one before. 10 less than 67 is 57.

questions.solution: Counting by fives means 5 more each time. 5 more than 70 is 75.

questions.stem: Which list counts by fives?
questions.solution: Counting by fives goes up 5 each time: 10, 15, 20, 25. The other lists count by ones, count by tens, or skip a number.

solve.work: 10, 15, 20, 25 goes up by 5 each time. 10,15,20,30 breaks the pattern; 10,11,12,13 is by ones; 10,20,30,40 is by tens.

questions.stem: Count by tens: 22, 32, ?, 52, 62. What number does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before. 10 more than 32 is 42.

questions.stem: Look at the numbers 24, 34, 44, 54. Which rule fits?
questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before it. The tens digit goes up by 1 and the ones digit stays 4.

solve.work: 24, 34, 44, 54 goes up by 10 each time: count up by tens.

questions.stem: Rae counts up by ones and says 119. Which number does she say next?
questions.solution: Count up by ones. 1 more than 119 is 120.

questions.stem: Dev counts back by ones: 112, 111, 110. What number does he say next?
questions.solution: Counting back by ones means 1 less each time. 1 less than 110 is 109.

questions.stem: A frog sits on lily pad 95. It jumps forward 3 pads, one pad at a time. Which lily pad is it on now?

questions.solution: After 99 comes 100.

questions.stem: A book has pages numbered 98, 99, ?, 101. What number is the ?

questions.stem: Which list is counting up by ones?
questions.solution: Counting up by ones adds 1 each time: 113, 114, 115, 116. The others go up by twos, tens or fives.

solve.work: 113, 114, 115, 116 goes up by 1 each time; others go by 10, 2, 5.

questions.stem: Nia counts back by ones and says 100. What number does she say next?
questions.solution: Counting back from 100, the next number is 99.

questions.stem: Which number is 1 less than 110?
questions.solution: Count back by one from 110 and you get 109.

questions.stem: A tower has 115 blocks. Kai takes off 2 blocks, one at a time. How many blocks are in the tower now?
questions.solution: Count back: 114, 113. The tower has 113 blocks.

questions.stem: Which list counts back by ones?
questions.solution: Counting back by ones takes 1 away each time. Only 104, 103, 102, 101 does that.

questions.stem: Cody has 25 cards. He gets 10 more, and then 10 more. How many cards does Cody have now?
questions.solution: Count up by tens from 25: 35, then 45.

questions.stem: Count up by tens: ?, 47, 57, 67. Which number is the ?
questions.solution: Going up by tens, the number before 47 is 10 less: 37.

questions.stem: What number is 10 more than 83?
questions.solution: The tens digit goes up by 1 and the ones digit stays 3: 93.

questions.stem: The rule is: add 10 each time. The first number is 6. Which list follows the rule?
questions.solution: Add 10 each time: 6, 16, 26, 36.

questions.stem: What number is 10 less than 94?
questions.solution: The tens digit goes down by 1 and the ones digit stays 4: 84.

questions.stem: Count back by tens from 119: 119, 109, 99. Which number comes next?
questions.solution: Take 10 from 99 to get 89.

questions.stem: A box has 76 crayons. Mia takes out 10 crayons, and then takes out 10 more. How many crayons are in the box now?
questions.solution: Count back by tens from 76: 66, then 56.

questions.stem: Count back by fives: 40, 35, 30. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Count back 5 from 30 to get 25.

questions.stem: Count by fives: 90, 95, ?, 105. Which number goes in the ?
questions.solution: 95 plus 5 is 100, and 100 plus 5 is 105.

questions.stem: Sara hops by fives on a number path. She starts on 45 and hops 3 times. What number does she land on?
questions.solution: Count by fives from 45: 50, 55, 60.

questions.stem: Which number is NOT said when you count by fives from 0?
questions.solution: Counting by fives only says numbers ending in 0 or 5. 48 ends in 8.

solve.work: Counting by fives from 0 gives numbers ending in 0 or 5; 48 is not said.

questions.stem: The numbers 41, 51, 61, 71 go up by the same amount each time. What is that amount?
questions.solution: Each number is 10 more than the one before.

questions.stem: Tia counts 100, 95, 90, 85. How does she count?
questions.solution: Each number is 5 less than the one before.

questions.stem: Ali counts by fives: 20, 25, 30, 36, 40. Which number did he say wrong?
questions.solution: After 30, counting by fives gives 35, not 36.

questions.stem: Which list does NOT count by tens?
questions.solution: In 40, 50, 60, 71 the last step is 11, not 10. The other lists add 10 each time.

solve.work: 60 to 71 is up 11, not 10; the others go up by 10.

questions.stem: Leo counts steps up a long stair. He is on step 98 and climbs 4 more steps, counting by ones. What step is he on?
questions.solution: Count up from 98: 99, 100, 101, 102. He is on step 102.

questions.stem: Start at 102. Count back by ones 5 times. Which number do you land on?
questions.solution: Count back from 102: 101, 100, 99, 98, 97. That is 5 steps, so you land on 97.

questions.stem: Start at 8. Count up by tens 5 times. What number do you land on?
questions.solution: Count up by tens from 8: 18, 28, 38, 48, 58. That is 5 times, so you land on 58.

solve.work: From 8 count up by tens 5 times: 18, 28, 38, 48, 58.

questions.stem: Count back by tens: 114, 104, 94, ?, 74. What number does the ? stand for?
questions.solution: Each number is 10 less than the one before. 10 less than 94 is 84, and 10 less than 84 is 74.

questions.stem: Count by fives: 85, 90, 95, 100. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Counting by fives means 5 more each time. 5 more than 100 is 105.

questions.stem: Kim hops by fives on a number path. She starts on 0 and hops 7 times. What number is she on?
questions.solution: Count by fives 7 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. She is on 35.

questions.stem: Which list counts up by tens?
questions.solution: Counting up by tens adds 10 each time: 56, 66, 76, 86. The other lists count by ones, count by fives, or jump 20 each time.

questions.stem: The numbers 5, 15, 25, 35 count by tens. What digit is in the ones place of every number?
questions.solution: Adding 10 changes the tens digit but not the ones digit. Every number ends in 5.

solve.work: 5, 15, 25, 35 all end in 5: the ones digit is 5.

questions.stem: Mia counts by fives from 0 to 120. Which number will she say?
questions.solution: Numbers said when counting by fives end in 0 or 5. Only 95 ends in 0 or 5.

solve.work: Counting by fives from 0 gives numbers ending in 0 or 5. Of 117, 103, 98, 95 only 95 ends in 0 or 5.

questions.stem: Jo counts back by tens. She says 120 first. What is the fifth number she says?
questions.solution: Count back by tens: 120, 110, 100, 90, 80. The fifth number is 80.

questions.stem: Start with 112. Say the next 6 numbers, counting up by ones. What is the last number you say?
questions.solution: Count: 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118. The sixth number is 118.

questions.stem: Eli counts up by ones from 104. Which list shows the next four numbers he says?
questions.solution: The next four numbers after 104 are 105, 106, 107 and 108. He does not say 104 again.

questions.stem: Jade has 100 beads on a string. She adds beads one at a time. After she adds 7 beads, how many beads are on the string?
questions.solution: Count up from 100 by ones seven times: 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107.

questions.stem: Which number is exactly 3 more than 108 when you count up by ones?
questions.solution: Count up 3 from 108: 109, 110, 111. The answer is 111.

questions.stem: A game starts with 120 points. Jo loses 1 point at a time and loses 6 points. How many points does she have now?
Count back by ones from 101. Which list shows the next four numbers?
questions.solution: After 101 comes 100, then 99, 98 and 97.

questions.stem: Count back by ones from 106 to 102. How many numbers do you say, counting 106 and 102 too?
questions.solution: The numbers are 106, 105, 104, 103, 102. That is 5 numbers.

questions.stem: Ava has 6 coins. Each day she gets 10 more coins. How many coins does she have after 4 days?
questions.solution: Count up by tens from 6: 16, 26, 36, 46.

questions.stem: Count up by tens from 75: 75, 85, 95. Which number comes next?
questions.solution: Add 10 to 95 to get 105.

questions.stem: A path has stones numbered 3, 13, 23, 33, and so on, counting by tens. What number is on the 7th stone?
questions.solution: Each stone is 10 more than the one before. The numbers are 3, 13, 23, 33, 43, 53, 63.

questions.stem: Ravi counts up by tens from 12. Which number will he say?
questions.solution: The numbers are 12, 22, 32, 42, 52. Only 52 is in the list.

solve.work: 12, 22, 32, 42, 52, ... Only 52 ends in 2 among the options.

questions.stem: Dev has 113 stickers. He gives away 10 stickers at a time, 4 times. How many stickers does he have left?
questions.solution: Count back by tens from 113: 103, 93, 83, 73.

questions.stem: Which number is 10 less than 105?
questions.solution: Count back by tens from 105: 95.

questions.stem: Count back by tens from 60 to 0. How many numbers do you say, counting 60 and 0 too?
questions.solution: The numbers are 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10, 0. That is 7 numbers.

questions.stem: Zed counts back by tens from 112. Which number will he say?
questions.solution: The numbers are 112, 102, 92, 82, 72, 62. Only 62 is in the list.

questions.stem: Leo has 70 points. In each round he scores 5 more points. After 6 rounds, how many points does he have?
questions.solution: Count by fives from 70: 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100.

questions.stem: Count by fives: 85, 90, two missing numbers, 105. Which pair fills in the missing numbers?
questions.solution: 90 plus 5 is 95, and 95 plus 5 is 100. Then 105 follows.

questions.stem: Count by fives from 0 up to 40. How many numbers do you say? Do not count 0.
questions.solution: The numbers are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. That is 8 numbers.

questions.stem: Pat counts by fives and says 100. Which number did Pat say right before 100?
questions.solution: Counting by fives, the number before 100 is 5 less: 95.

questions.stem: Zoe counts by fives from 0. Wes counts by tens from 0. Which number do both children say?
questions.solution: Wes says only numbers like 10, 20, 30, 40. Zoe says 40 too, but not the others.

questions.stem: Rae counts by fives from 70: 70, 75, 80, and so on. How many numbers does she say from 70 up to 100, counting 70 and 100?
questions.solution: The numbers are 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100. That is 7 numbers.

questions.stem: Eli counts up by tens from 3: 3, 13, 23, 33, 43. Which sentence is true?
choices: The ones digit is 3 in every number
The tens digit is 3 in every number
The ones digit goes up by 1 each time
questions.answer: The ones digit is 3 in every number
questions.solution: Adding 10 changes only the tens digit. The ones digit stays 3.

solve.answer: The ones digit is 3 in every number

questions.stem: Sue counts back by tens: 120, 110, 100, 90. She keeps going until she says 0. How many numbers does she say after 90?

questions.solution: 4 tens is 40. 12 ones is 12. 40 and 12 make 52. The others make 62, 42 and 25.

solve.work: 4 tens and 2 ones = 42; 2 tens and 5 ones = 25; 5 tens and 12 ones = 62; 4 tens and 12 ones = 40 + 12 = 52. Only the last is 52.

questions.skill: Tens and ones to a number
questions.stem: A number has 7 ones. It has 2 more tens than ones. What is the number?
questions.solution: The number has 7 ones. 2 more than 7 is 9, so it has 9 tens. 9 tens and 7 ones is 97.

solve.work: 7 ones; tens = 7 + 2 = 9 tens. 9 tens and 7 ones = 97.

questions.skill: Tens and ones to a number
questions.stem: Dan has 4 sticks of ten and 5 loose cubes. Each stick has 10 cubes. He gets 1 more stick. How many cubes does he have now?
questions.solution: 4 sticks and 1 more stick make 5 sticks, which is 50 cubes. Add the 5 loose cubes to get 55.

solve.work: 4 sticks + 5 loose = 45. One more stick: 5 sticks and 5 loose = 55.

questions.solution: There are seven 10s. Seven tens make 70. 70 and 8 make 78.

questions.skill: Other ways to make a number
questions.stem: Which is NOT another way to show 46?
questions.solution: 4 tens and 6 ones is 46. 3 tens and 16 ones is 30 + 16, which is 46. 2 tens and 26 ones is 20 + 26, which is 46. 6 tens and 4 ones is 64, not 46.

solve.work: 2 tens and 26 ones = 20 + 26 = 46; 4 tens and 6 ones = 46; 6 tens and 4 ones = 64; 3 tens and 16 ones = 30 + 16 = 46. Only 6 tens and 4 ones is not 46.

questions.stem: In the number 77, which sentence is true?
choices: The 7 on the left is worth 70 and the 7 on the right is worth 7.
The 7 on the left is worth 7 and the 7 on the right is worth 70.
questions.answer: The 7 on the left is worth 70 and the 7 on the right is worth 7.
questions.solution: The left 7 is in the tens place, so it is 7 tens, or 70. The right 7 is in the ones place, so it is worth 7.

solve.answer: The 7 on the left is worth 70 and the 7 on the right is worth 7.
solve.work: 77 = 7 tens and 7 ones: the left 7 is in the tens place (70), the right 7 in the ones place (7).

questions.skill: Make a ten from ten ones
questions.stem: A box holds 10 pencils. Rosa has 5 full boxes and 10 loose pencils. She puts the 10 loose pencils in another box. How many full boxes does she have now?
questions.solution: 10 loose pencils fill 1 more box. 5 boxes and 1 more box make 6 full boxes.

solve.work: 5 full boxes, plus 10 loose pencils fill 1 more box: 5 + 1 = 6 full boxes.

questions.skill: Other ways to make a number
questions.stem: Max says 90 is 9 tens and 0 ones. Ana says 90 is 8 tens and 10 ones. Who is right?
questions.solution: 9 tens is 90. 8 tens and 10 ones is 80 + 10, which is also 90. 10 ones can be traded for 1 ten, so both ways show 90.

solve.work: 9 tens and 0 ones = 90. 8 tens and 10 ones = 80 + 10 = 90. Both are right.

questions.stem: Lily has 6 tens and 3 ones. She trades 1 ten for 10 ones. How many ones does she have now?
questions.solution: 1 ten is 10 ones. After the trade she has 5 tens and 3 + 10 ones, which is 13 ones.

solve.work: 6 tens and 3 ones = 63. Trading 1 ten for 10 ones: 5 tens and 3 + 10 = 13 ones.

questions.skill: Make a ten from ten ones
questions.stem: A tray holds 10 muffins. Pam has 4 full trays and 13 more muffins. She puts 10 of the 13 on a new tray. How many full trays does she have now?
questions.solution: 10 of the loose muffins make 1 more full tray. 4 trays and 1 more tray make 5 full trays.

solve.work: 4 full trays + 1 new full tray = 5 (3 left over).

questions.skill: Make a ten from ten ones
questions.stem: Kai has 8 tens and 10 ones. He trades the 10 ones for tens. How many tens does he have now?
questions.solution: 10 ones make 1 ten. 8 tens and 1 more ten make 9 tens.

questions.solution: The number of ones is 3 and 4 more, which is 7. So the number has 3 tens and 7 ones: 37.

questions.solution: 5 tens and 2 ones is 52. 3 more ones make 55.

questions.solution: 3 bars and 2 bars make 5 bars, which is 50 cubes. 50 and 7 loose cubes make 57.

questions.solution: 50 has 5 tens and 80 has 8 tens. 5 tens is fewer, so Nina has fewer. She has 50 pennies.

questions.solution: 9 has no tens. 15 has 1 ten, 20 has 2 tens and 31 has 3 tens. So 9 has the fewest.

questions.stem: Five children have 38, 83, 29, 92 and 74 stickers. Type the second-greatest number of stickers.
questions.solution: In order from greatest the numbers are 92, 83, 74, 38 and 29. The second-greatest is 83.

questions.stem: Which number is greater than all three of 41, 58 and 36?
questions.solution: The greatest of the three is 58. 62 is greater than 58. The other choices are less than 58.

questions.skill: Compare numbers with the same tens
questions.stem: Which number is more than 71 and less than 73?
questions.solution: The only whole number after 71 and before 73 is 72.

questions.skill: Compare numbers with the same tens
questions.stem: Type the greatest number: 87, 78, 88 or 79.
questions.solution: 87 and 88 have 8 tens, which is more than the 7 tens in 78 and 79. Of 87 and 88, 88 has more ones.

questions.skill: Compare numbers with the same tens
questions.stem: The numbers 92, 98 and 95 are put in order. Type the number in the middle.
questions.solution: All have 9 tens. The ones are 2, 8 and 5. The order is 92, 95, 98, so the middle number is 95.

questions.skill: Compare numbers with the same tens

choices: He compared the tens first. He should compare the ones first.
He should have said 83 is equal to 79.
He should have added the two numbers.
He compared the ones first. He should compare the tens first.
questions.answer: He compared the ones first. He should compare the tens first.
questions.solution: 83 has 8 tens and 79 has 7 tens. Compare the tens first: 8 tens is more than 7 tens, so 83 is greater.

solve.answer: He compared the ones first. He should compare the tens first.
solve.work: 8 tens > 7 tens so 83 > 79; he compared ones first.

questions.stem: Which sentence compares $30 + 12$ and $40 + 1$ correctly?
questions.solution: $30 + 12$ is 42 and $40 + 1$ is 41. 42 is greater than 41. Also, $30 + 1$ is 31, which is less than 42.

questions.stem: A number has 7 tens and some ones. It is less than 74. Type the greatest number of ones it can have.
questions.solution: The number is 70, 71, 72 or 73. The greatest number of ones is 3.

questions.stem: Which sentence compares 29 and 30 correctly?
questions.solution: 29 has 2 tens and 30 has 3 tens. 29 is less than 30. 92 is greater than 30.

questions.stem: Four children have 45, 54, 40 and 50 stickers. Which list is in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: All have 4 or 5 tens. 40 and 45 have 4 tens and 40 has fewer ones. 50 and 54 have 5 tens and 50 has fewer ones. The order is 40, 45, 50, 54.

questions.stem: Put 63, 36, 66 and 33 in order from least to greatest. Type the third number.
questions.solution: The order is 33, 36, 63, 66. The third number is 63.

questions.stem: Which list is NOT in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: In 27, 72, 70, 91 the number 70 comes after 72, but 70 is less than 72. The other lists are in order.

questions.solution: 1 less than 63 is 62. It fits in order between 57 and 63.

questions.skill: Use a number line to compare numbers
questions.stem: On a number line, a dot is to the right of 48 and to the left of 52. Which number could the dot be?
questions.solution: The dot is at a number greater than 48 and less than 52. 50 fits. 47 and 48 are too small and 53 is too big.

questions.skill: Use a number line to compare numbers
questions.stem: A dot is at 56 on a number line. A second dot is 10 to the right of it. Type the number of the second dot.
questions.solution: Moving right means getting greater. 56 and 10 more is 66.

questions.skill: Use a number line to compare numbers
questions.stem: Dots on a number line are at 34, 29, 41 and 38. Bigger numbers are to the right. Which dot is farthest from the right end?
questions.solution: The dot farthest from the right end is the one farthest to the left. That is the least number, 29.

solve.work: Farthest from right end = leftmost = smallest = 29.

questions.skill: Estimate with benchmarks on a number line
questions.stem: A number line has a mark at every 10. A dot is exactly halfway between the marks 60 and 70. Type its number.
questions.solution: Halfway between 60 and 70 is 5 more than 60. That is 65.

questions.skill: Estimate with benchmarks on a number line
questions.stem: A number line goes from 0 to 100. A dot is just to the left of the 100 end. Which number could it be?
questions.solution: Just to the left of 100 means a little less than 100. 97 is close to 100. The others are far from it.

questions.stem: I am a number between 50 and 70. My tens digit is 5 and my ones digit is 4. Next, I get 10 more. What number do I have?
questions.solution: I am 54. 10 more than 54 is 64.

questions.stem: I am less than 40. I have more than 2 tens. My ones digit is 5. Which number am I?
questions.solution: More than 2 tens and less than 40 means 3 tens. With 5 ones I am 35.

questions.stem: I have 2 digits. My tens digit is 4 more than my ones digit. My ones digit is 3. What number am I?
questions.solution: The ones digit is 3. The tens digit is 4 more, which is 7. I am 73.

questions.skill: Compare numbers in tens and ones
questions.stem: Eve has 3 tens and 14 ones of beads. Fay has 4 tens and 2 ones. Type the number of beads the child with more has.
questions.solution: Eve has 3 tens and 14 ones, which is 30 and 14, or 44. Fay has 42. 44 is greater than 42, so Eve has more: 44.

questions.stem: Zed counts on to find $9 + 3$. He starts at 9 and counts on 3 more. What number does he end on?
questions.solution: Start at 9 and count on 3: 10, 11, 12. He ends on 12.

solve.work: Start at 9, count on 3: 10, 11, 12. Ends on 12.

questions.stem: Which shows how to count on to find $5 + 3$?
questions.solution: To count on, start at the first number and say the next numbers up. For $5 + 3$, start at 5 and say 6, 7, 8. The last number, 8, is the answer.

solve.work: Counting on from 5 by 3 more: say 6, 7, 8 (5 + 3 = 8). '4, 3, 2' counts back; '5, 6, 7' repeats the start; '6, 7' is only 2 more.

questions.stem: Ana has 6 red cubes and 6 blue cubes. How many cubes does she have in all?
questions.solution: The same number twice is a doubles fact. $6 + 6 = 12$.

questions.stem: $8 + ? = 10$. What is the ?
questions.solution: 8 and 2 make 10, so $8 + 2 = 10$. The ? is 2.

questions.solution: $4 + 3 = 7$, so if you take 3 away from 7, 4 is left. $7 - 3 = 4$.

questions.stem: Start at 8 and count back 3. What number do you end on?
questions.solution: Count back 3 from 8: 7, 6, 5. Do not say 8 as one of the 3 counts. You end on 5.

questions.stem: Tom has 7 toy cars. His dad gives him 4 more. How many toy cars does Tom have now?
questions.solution: Tom has 7 and gets 4 more, so add: $7 + 4 = 11$. Count on from 7: 8, 9, 10, 11.

questions.solution: 5 birds leave, so take away: $12 - 5 = 7$. Check: $7 + 5 = 12$.

questions.solution: Count on 2 from 6: 7, 8. So $2 + 6 = 8$. The other sentences have a total that is too small or too big, or they take away instead of adding.

questions.solution: Start at 6 and count on 2: 7, 8. She ends on 8.

questions.solution: Start at 9 and count on 2: 10, 11. So $2 + 9 = 11$.

questions.solution: 7 and 3 make 10, so she needs 3 more.

questions.solution: To find $9 - 4$, think: 4 plus what is 9? $4 + 5 = 9$, so $9 - 4 = 5$.

questions.solution: 4 plus 6 is 10, so 6 cubes are hidden.

questions.solution: 5 plus 4 is 9, so $9 - 5 = 4$.

questions.solution: Take away: $10 - 3 = 7$.

questions.solution: 6 plus how many is 10? $6 + 4 = 10$, so she got 4 stars.

questions.solution: 8 is 1 more than 7, so $7 + 8$ is 1 more than $7 + 7$. 14 and 1 more is 15.

questions.solution: $8 + 2 = 10$. The 5 was split into 2 and 3, so 3 is left over. $10 + 3 = 13$. So $8 + 5 = 13$.

questions.solution: $13 - 6$ asks what you add to 6 to get 13. So $6 + ? = 13$ helps. The ? is 7, so $13 - 6 = 7$.

solve.work: Subtraction as an unknown addend: 13 - 6 = ? is the same as 6 + ? = 13 (? = 7). The other options do not give 7.

questions.stem: What is $14 - 5$?
questions.solution: Think $5 + ? = 14$. Since $5 + 9 = 14$, we have $14 - 5 = 9$. Or take 4 from 14 to get 10, then take 1 more to get 9.

questions.solution: Put the shells together: $9 + 6$. $9 + 1 = 10$, and 5 more makes 15. They have 15 shells.

questions.stem: A box has 16 crayons. 7 of the crayons are red. The rest are blue. How many crayons are blue?
questions.solution: Take the red ones away from all of the crayons: $16 - 7 = 9$. Check: $7 + 9 = 16$.

questions.skill: Word problem with the start or the change unknown
questions.stem: Eli has 8 books. He gets some more books. Now he has 13 books. How many books did he get?
questions.solution: He started with 8 and ended with 13, so $8 + ? = 13$. Since $8 + 5 = 13$, he got 5 books.

questions.solution: Start at the bigger number, 13, and count on 2: 14, 15. So $2 + 13 = 15$.

questions.solution: $9$ is one more than 8, so $8 + 9$ is $8 + 8$ and 1 more: $16 + 1 = 17$.

questions.solution: Take 1 from the 6 to make 10 with the 9. Then $10 + 5 = 15$.

questions.solution: Move 2 from the 7 to the 8: $8 + 7 = 10 + 5 = 15$.

questions.solution: 5 plus 8 is 13, so Sue has 8 cards left.

questions.solution: 5 longer than 9 is $9 + 5 = 14$.

questions.solution: Add 3 and 7 to make 10, then $10 + 6 = 16$.

Add 4 and 6 to make 10, then add 8

solve.work: Equal groups making 18: 9 + 9 = 18, so 9 on each plate.

questions.stem: Kim makes a ten to add $7 + 5$. She takes some from the 5 and gives them to the 7 to make 10. How many does she take from the 5?
questions.solution: She needs 10 with the 7. $7 + 3 = 10$, so she takes 3 from the 5. That leaves 2, and $10 + 2 = 12$.

solve.work: 7 needs 3 to make 10, so she takes 3 from the 5 (7 + 3 = 10, 10 + 2 = 12).

questions.stem: $15 - ? = 8$. Think of $8 + ? = 15$. What is the ?
questions.solution: $15 - ? = 8$ means that 8 plus the ? makes 15. $8 + 7 = 15$, so the ? is 7.

questions.solution: Think $9 + ? = 17$. Since $9 + 8 = 17$, we have $17 - 9 = 8$. Or take 7 from 17 to get 10, then take 2 more to get 8.

questions.solution: Ola said 5 numbers after 9, so Ola added 5.

questions.solution: Raj has $5 + 5 = 10$. Together: $5 + 10 = 15$.
